hero.title: Master's in Computer Engineering in Mauritius for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: Pursue an affordable, internationally accredited Master's in Computer and Systems Engineering in Mauritius, gaining advanced expertise in embedded hardware and IoT systems with streamlined visa processing.

overview: Mauritius offers a strategic, accessible education destination for international graduate engineering students in the Indian Ocean region, providing internationally recognized postgraduate degree programs in an English-speaking, multicultural environment. Studying a master's in Computer Engineering in Mauritius combines advanced technical instruction with highly competitive tuition and living costs.

Mauritian universities and international branch campuses deliver 1- to 2-year Master of Science (MSc) and Master of Engineering programs in Computer Systems and Embedded Technologies. Coursework covers Advanced Microcontroller Design, Embedded Systems Architecture, Industrial IoT Hardware, and Telecommunications Systems, incorporating practical laboratory research and industry capstone design projects.

With competitive annual tuition fees (typically $3,000 to $9,000 USD), affordable student accommodation, and a streamlined visa application process with no embassy interviews, Mauritius represents a high-value destination. Upon graduation, international students can transition into employment through the Economic Development Board (EDB) Young Professional Occupation Permit (YPOP) or standard Occupation Permit schemes subject to qualifying employer sponsorship.

7. Admission Process for Computer Engineering in Mauritius

Students can follow these steps when applying for a suitable postgraduate computing or engineering programme. Those planning to Study Computer Engineering in Mauritius should first make sure that the selected course matches their intended area of study.

items.title: Identify the right specialisation: Decide whether you want to focus on computer hardware, embedded systems, AI, software, networking or applied computing.

sections.title: Compare available courses: Review the official programme descriptions, modules and degree titles.
Check eligibility: Confirm that your bachelor’s degree and academic results meet the admission requirements.
Verify tuition and duration: Ask about international fees, programme mode and additional charges.
Prepare your application: Collect transcripts, certificates, passport details and other required documents.
Submit the application: Apply through the university’s official admissions portal.

items: 8. Further Study Options After a Master’s in Computer Engineering
After completing a relevant master’s degree, graduates may consider further study or research in specialised areas such as:
PhD in Computer Engineering: Research into computing hardware, architecture, embedded systems or related technologies.
PhD in Computer Science: Advanced research in algorithms, computing systems, AI or software.
Research in Artificial Intelligence: Explore machine learning, intelligent systems and applied AI.
Research in Embedded Systems and IoT: Study connected devices, sensors, microcontrollers and integrated systems.
Research in Cybersecurity: Investigate hardware security, network protection and secure computing.
Advanced research in Telecommunications: Explore communication systems and network technologies.
Admission to research programmes depends on the candidate’s qualifications, research proposal, academic record and availability of a suitable supervisor.
9. Career Opportunities After Computer Engineering

A relevant postgraduate qualification can support careers across computing, electronics and technology. The specific roles available depend on the degree, practical experience and employer requirements. Students considering a Master’s in Computer Engineering in Mauritius for Indian Students should evaluate the career relevance of the programme before choosing a related qualification.
Potential career paths include:
Computer systems engineer: Works with computer systems and related infrastructure.
Embedded systems engineer: Develops software and integrated systems for devices and equipment.
Hardware design engineer: Works on digital circuits, electronic components or computing hardware, subject to suitable technical training.
AI engineer: Develops or implements AI-based systems.
Systems architect: Designs the structure and integration of complex technology systems.
Network engineer: Designs, configures and maintains computer networks.
Software engineer: Develops, tests and maintains software applications.
Research engineer: Supports technical research, prototyping and product development.

Students targeting hardware-focused roles should look for relevant modules and practical experience in digital electronics, computer architecture, embedded systems and hardware design. A general computing degree may not provide the same depth in these areas.

11. Frequently Asked Questions
1. Is a Master’s in Computer Engineering available in Mauritius?

A dedicated Master’s in Computer Engineering was not found in the University of Mauritius’s published postgraduate programme list for 2026–2027. Related options include the MSc in Artificial Intelligence, MSc in Software Project Management and MSc in Applied Computing and Digital Technologies. Students researching a Master’s in Computer Engineering in Mauritius for Indian Students should verify the latest programme availability directly with universities.
2. Which university offers a related master’s programme?

The Open University of Mauritius offers an MSc in Applied Computing and Digital Technologies. The University of Mauritius offers postgraduate programmes in Artificial Intelligence and Software Project Management. These programmes have different curricula and should not be considered direct substitutes for a Computer Engineering degree.

Check the university for the current fee schedule and other Master’s in Computer Engineering Fees in Mauritius information before making a financial decision.
4. What are the living expenses for international students in Mauritius?

The University of Mauritius estimates monthly living expenses of approximately MUR 15,000–25,000, or about ₹28,500–₹47,500 using the illustrative exchange rate in this article. Actual costs vary according to accommodation and lifestyle.
5. What career opportunities are available after studying Computer Engineering?

Depending on the course and practical skills developed, graduates may pursue roles in embedded systems, computer systems, AI, networking, software development, hardware design or technology research. Hardware-focused roles may require specialised modules and hands-on experience.
